item.title: #3585912: STDIO tool calls execute without an authenticated user, so permission-gated tools fail
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3585912 · 1 contributor · 22 comments
  • Followers: 1

Summary

Previously, drush mcp:server (the STDIO transport used by AI clients like Claude Desktop) ran every tool call as the anonymous user, so any permission-gated tool (most entity or configuration reads/writes) silently failed access checks. The command now requires a Drupal account argument, a user name or numeric ID, and runs the whole session as that account, so permission checks evaluate correctly. Passing 0 still allows an explicit anonymous session. Existing MCP client configurations and manual invocations that call mcp:server with no argument will now fail with an error rather than silently running as anonymous, so they need to be updated to pass an account. Running the command from an interactive terminal without an argument now opens a user picker instead of failing.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Requirements: Minimum Drush version for the STDIO transport raised from 12.x to 13.
  • API change: drush mcp:server now takes a required account argument (user name or numeric ID, or 0 for anonymous); invocations that omit it now error instead of running as anonymous.

Technical details

The fix is in McpServerCommands::server(), which gained a required account positional argument. loadAccount() resolves it: '0' becomes an AnonymousUserSession, an all-digit value loads the user by ID, anything else is looked up by user name via entity_type.manager's user storage; blocked or unresolvable accounts throw before the transport is created. The resolved account is applied with the account_switcher service (AccountSwitcherInterface::switchTo()), and switchBack() runs in a finally block so the process-global account is always restored.

A Drush #[CLI\Hook(type: HookManager::INTERACT, ...)] hook, interactAccount(), handles the case where the argument is omitted: if STDIN is a TTY (a real terminal, not an MCP client's pipes), it prompts with $this->io()->search() against matchUsers() (a fuzzy, access-check-free lookup over active user names); otherwise Symfony's normal missing-argument error is reported on STDERR before the server is built, so nothing corrupts the STDIO transport. The README.md and the mcp_server_test module's new test_current_user tool (which reports the acting uid, name, and a permission check) were added to support this. The change also bumps the documented minimum Drush version for STDIO to 13.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">Update any MCP client configuration or manual invocation of the STDIO transport to pass an account:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "drupal": {
      "command": "vendor/bin/drush",
      "args": ["mcp:server", "admin"]
    }
  }
}

or from the shell:

drush mcp:server admin

Use drush mcp:server 0 to keep running as anonymous. Also confirm the site runs Drush 13 or higher for the STDIO transport.

item.title: #3583023: Emit the JSON Schema from tool:info and pass a Drush invoker
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583023 · 1 contributor · 14 comments

Summary

The Tool module's drush tool:info <id> --format=json command previously reduced every input and output to a bare data type (string, map, etc.), with no way to see that a field only accepts a fixed set of values, or what keys a map input expects. Now the JSON output also includes input_schema and output_schema keys with the full JSON Schema for the tool, so a script or AI agent reading this command's output can discover enum choices, numeric ranges, formats, and nested map properties before invoking the tool. The human-readable table and markdown output formats gained a matching Constraints column, and now show map inputs' individual properties as indented sub-rows, so all three output formats stay in sync.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: tool:info --format=json gains input_schema and output_schema keys carrying the full JSON Schema (enums, min/max, map properties) for a tool's inputs and outputs, alongside the unchanged flat inputs/outputs keys.

Technical details

The fix routes tool:info through the same tool.definition_serializer (ToolDefinitionSerializer) that already powers the MCP bridge and AI connector, instead of hand-building arrays. Because that serializer normalizes a tool instance rather than a bare definition (ToolDefinitionNormalizeEvent subscribers key off the invoker), ToolInfoCommand now instantiates the tool via a new Drupal\tool\Drush\DrushInvoker (@internal, ID drush, no capabilities) and calls $serializer->normalizeInputSchema($tool, include_locked: TRUE) and normalizeOutputDefinitions($tool) in a new buildSchemas() helper. ToolRunCommand::executeTool() was also switched from a bare createInstance($tool_id) to passing DrushInvoker::create(), so both commands now identify themselves consistently to invoker-aware subscribers. A one-shot Drush invoker declares no capabilities (in particular no EntitiesAsHandles), unlike the MCP/AI connector invokers, since a CLI process has no session to hold entity handles.

The table and markdown renderers were reworked around the same schema data via new private helpers (buildInputRows(), buildPropertyRows(), summarizeConstraints(), schemaType()) so the three output formats can't drift: summarizeConstraints() reads enum, const, format, pattern, minimum/maximum, min/maxLength, min/maxItems off a schema node, and buildPropertyRows() recurses into a map input's properties (or a multiple map's items.properties) to emit indented └ property rows. The tool.definition_serializer service is wired with the optional @?serializer argument, since Tool doesn't hard-depend on core's serialization module; note that in this landed version, if that service is unavailable ToolDefinitionSerializer throws LogicException and tool:info does not catch it (the issue's proposal to degrade gracefully by omitting the schema keys and printing a stderr notice is not present in the merged code). Tests in ToolInfoCommandTest were extended against schema_matrix_tool, asserting enum, properties, required, and minimum/maximum show up correctly in input_schema while the flat inputs/outputs keys stay unchanged.

item.title: #3585923: Session lock is released before streamed (SSE) responses finish
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Version: 2.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3585923 · 1 contributor · 6 comments

Summary

MCP Server's per-session lock, introduced to stop two requests from touching the same session at once, was being released too early for streamed (SSE) responses. Because the SDK does its actual work later, while the response is being sent, a second request could sneak in and read or write session state while the first request was still streaming. On PostgreSQL sites using the database lock backend this also produced a nastier symptom: a tool that opened a database transaction and then suspended could have its later rollback resurrect the just-deleted lock row, forcing the next request on that session to wait out the entire lock lease and hit client-side timeouts. This is fixed so the lock is now held for the full duration of the streamed response.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: Session lock could be released while an SSE (streamed) response was still running, letting a concurrent request read or write the same MCP session's state.

Technical details

The fix is in McpServerController::handle(). Previously the lock release lived only in the method's finally block, which runs as soon as the controller returns, before a StreamedResponse's callback has actually executed. Now, when the transport's PSR response body is not seekable (the SSE path), the controller wraps the StreamedResponse's existing callback in a new closure that calls the original callback and releases $lock_name in its own finally, so the lock lives until the SDK's Fiber-driven stream actually completes or throws. A new $release_lock flag tells the controller's outer finally to skip releasing the lock itself in that case, since the wrapped callback now owns that responsibility. Non-streamed responses and exceptions thrown before a response is produced still release the lock the old way. If a streamed response is constructed but never sent, its callback never runs and thus never releases the lock explicitly. That case relies on LockBackendInterface::releaseAll(), which DatabaseLockBackend registers as a shutdown function, as covered by the new testUnsentStreamedResponseLockIsFreedByReleaseAll kernel test. A companion test, testStreamedResponseHoldsSessionLockUntilSent, drives a tool that suspends inside a Fiber and a real DatabaseLockBackend, asserting the lock is still held after the controller returns and only released once $response->sendContent() finishes.

item.title: #3585927: Remove McpToolSamplingTrait
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 2.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3585927 · 1 contributor · 5 comments

Summary

The mcp_server module removed McpToolSamplingTrait, a convenience helper that tool plugins could use to ask the AI client to generate text (LLM "sampling"). The trait, its test coverage, and the test-only SamplingEchoTool fixture are gone. This was done because the underlying mcp/sdk package (0.8+) marked its own Sampling feature as deprecated, and the module, still in beta, does not carry deprecated code forward with a transition period. Sites and custom tools that used this trait need to update their code; everything else about the module is unaffected.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Drupal\mcp_server\Traits\McpToolSamplingTrait and its sample() helper were removed; tools that requested LLM sampling must call ClientGateway::sample() directly.
  • Deprecation: No deprecation period was provided before removal, per the module's beta no-BC-layers policy.

Technical details

The fix deletes src/Traits/McpToolSamplingTrait.php, its kernel test tests/src/Kernel/Traits/McpToolSamplingTraitTest.php, and the fixture tests/modules/mcp_server_test/src/Plugin/mcp_server/Tool/SamplingEchoTool.php that exercised it. These were the only source of the 7 PHPStan errors flagged after mcp/sdk ^0.8 was allowed in #3585925 (mcp/sdk 0.8 deprecated SamplingMessage/CreateSamplingMessageResult usage and ClientGateway::sample() under SEP-2577).

ClientGatewayAwareInterface (src/ClientGatewayAwareInterface.php) is kept as is, its docblock updated to drop the sampling-specific framing and describe the gateway more generally (progress reporting, elicitation), since those SDK features are not deprecated. Any tool that still needs sampling now calls $gateway->sample() directly on the ClientGateway instance passed into execute(), which surfaces the SDK's own @deprecated notice in PHPStan rather than having it masked by the trait. The issue notes mcp_server_tool_bridge was the only known consumer, and only in test fixtures, addressed separately in that project's merge request 14.

Upgrade

Replace any use of McpToolSamplingTrait::sample() with a direct call on the ClientGateway passed into execute():

// Before:
use Drupal\mcp_server\Traits\McpToolSamplingTrait;

final class MyTool extends ToolPluginBase implements ClientGatewayAwareInterface {
  use McpToolSamplingTrait;

  public function execute(array $arguments, ClientGateway $gateway): mixed {
    $this->setClientGateway($gateway);
    $result = $this->sample($arguments['prompt'] ?? '', 500);
    // ...
  }
}

// After:
final class MyTool extends ToolPluginBase {
  public function execute(array $arguments, ClientGateway $gateway): mixed {
    $result = $gateway->sample($arguments['prompt'] ?? '', 500);
    // ...
  }
}

Note that mcp/sdk's ClientGateway::sample() itself is deprecated (earliest removal 2027-07-28 per SEP-2577), so PHPStan will now report that deprecation directly at the call site instead of it being hidden by the trait.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: September 17, 2026

item.title: #3436728: Check the status of a consumer
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 6.1.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 9 files, +176/−7 · php +175/−6 · json +1/−1
  • Diff: 14da180
  • Discussion: #3436728 · 7 contributors · 25 comments
  • Followers: 8
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 7 contributors

Summary

Simple OAuth now checks whether an OAuth client (a "consumer" entity) is published before granting it access. Previously, unpublishing a consumer did not actually stop it from working: it could still request new access tokens via the client credentials or refresh token grants, and tokens it had already obtained kept working against protected resources. Now an unpublished consumer is treated as if it doesn't exist: attempts to obtain a token fail with an invalid_client error, and requests bearing a token issued by a now-disabled client are rejected with "The client is disabled." The client selection dropdown in the client credentials token creation form also stops listing unpublished consumers.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: Unpublished (disabled) consumers can no longer obtain new OAuth tokens or use previously issued bearer tokens; this closes an access control gap.
  • Requirements: Minimum drupal/consumers dependency raised to ^1.24 for the consumer entity status field.

Technical details

The fix relies on the status field added to the consumer entity by the consumers module (see #3436723), and bumps the drupal/consumers dependency to ^1.24 to guarantee its availability.

ClientRepository::getClientEntity() now adds 'status' => 1 to the loadByProperties() lookup used to find a consumer by client_id, so an unpublished consumer resolves to no client entity at all, which makes validateClient() return FALSE for both the client credentials and refresh token grant types. Oauth2ClientCredentialsTokenCreateForm applies the same status condition to the client entity query and the storage lookup used during validation, so unpublished consumers disappear from the form's client list.

For tokens issued before a consumer was unpublished, SimpleOauthAuthenticationProvider::authenticate() now calls $account->getConsumer()->isPublished() and throws an OAuthUnauthorizedHttpException ("The client is disabled.") when it returns FALSE, so previously granted bearer tokens stop working as soon as their consumer is disabled. Kernel tests cover all three paths: rejecting an unpublished client at the client credentials grant, at the refresh token grant, and at resource access with an already-issued bearer token.

Upgrade

Update the drupal/consumers dependency to at least 1.24, which is where the consumer status field this feature relies on was introduced:

"drupal/consumers": "^1.24",

Any code relying on a disabled/unpublished consumer still being able to authenticate or use previously issued tokens will now be blocked; disable a consumer only when access should actually be revoked.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: March 28, 2024
  • Committed: September 18, 2026 (2 years later)

Key contributors

  • gorkagr (Erasmus Student Network)
  • bojan_dev
  • scott falconer (Acquia)
  • attilatilman (Acquia)
  • mglaman (Acquia)

Collaboration

The issue was postponed for a long time waiting on the consumers module to gain a status field (#3436723). Once that landed, bojan_dev pointed out that getClientEntity() could simply be restricted to loading published consumers, and later released consumers 1.23/pushed for 1.24 to make the status field available. attilatilman then implemented the fix in MR !234, adding kernel test coverage for the client credentials grant, refresh token grant, and already-issued bearer tokens, plus a few unrelated pre-existing issues found while working on the branch (missing type hints, a mismatched deprecation message, and a Drupal 11.4 compatibility fix). scott falconer tested the change and confirmed it caught the case correctly, and mglaman gave RTBC.

item.title: #3585924: Drop mcp/sdk ^0.6 and require 0.7.1
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 2.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3585924 · 1 contributor · 6 comments

Summary

The mcp_server module's dependency on the mcp/sdk package is tightened to require version 0.7.1 or newer. The previous constraint still allowed ^0.6 and 0.7.0, both of which are covered by security advisory CVE-2026-53965. Sites that run composer update will now be prevented from installing (or keeping) a vulnerable mcp/sdk release, and sites that had disabled Composer's advisory check were previously left exposed. There is no code change in the module itself.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: The mcp/sdk composer constraint now requires ^0.7.1 || ^0.8, excluding the ^0.6 line and the 0.7.0 release, both covered by CVE-2026-53965.

Technical details

A prior fix (#3585916) had temporarily widened the constraint to ^0.6 || ^0.7 to unblock fresh installs from Composer's advisory blocking, but 0.6.0 (the only 0.6 release) and 0.7.0 are both within the Packagist advisory range >=0.5.0,<0.7.1. This issue removes ^0.6 entirely and raises the 0.7 floor to 0.7.1, the first release outside the advisory range. The change is a one-line edit to the require.mcp/sdk constraint in composer.json; the module has no 0.6-specific code paths, so no PHP code was touched.

Upgrade

Run composer update drupal/mcp_server mcp/sdk to pick up the new constraint. Confirm the installed mcp/sdk version satisfies:

"mcp/sdk": "^0.7.1 || ^0.8"

If your project's lock file still resolves to 0.6.0 or 0.7.0, update it to clear CVE-2026-53965.

item.title: #3585879: Use a lock for sessions to handle concurrency issue with session data
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3585879 · 1 contributor · 7 comments

Summary

The MCP Server module's HTTP controller now serializes concurrent requests that belong to the same MCP session, preventing session data corruption. Previously, if two requests for the same Mcp-Session-Id arrived at once (for example, two tool calls in flight at the same time), each worker could read stale session state and overwrite the other's changes when saving, silently corrupting the session's protocol state. Sites using the MCP Server module with concurrent clients will now see occasional brief waits, or in the worst case a 503 Service Unavailable response with a Retry-After header, instead of silent data corruption.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The underlying issue traces to the PHP MCP SDK (see modelcontextprotocol/php-sdk#275), which stores protocol state (outgoing queue, request counter, pending requests) in a shared session blob using an unlocked read-modify-write pattern. McpServerController::handle() now derives a lock name from the request's Mcp-Session-Id header, hashed with hash('sha256', ...) to keep the lock key bounded and safe regardless of client-supplied header content, and stored under the mcp_session: prefix.

Before invoking $server->run($transport), the controller attempts $this->lock->acquire($lock_name); on failure it calls $this->lock->wait($lock_name) and retries once, throwing a ServiceUnavailableHttpException (with retryAfter: 1) if the lock still cannot be obtained. The lock is released in a finally block via $this->lock->release($lock_name). Requests without a session ID (such as initialize) skip locking entirely since there is no shared state yet to protect. The lock is injected via the new LockBackendInterface $lock constructor parameter, wired to Drupal's core lock service in create().

Note that this initial implementation released the lock as soon as $server->run() returned, which was not correct for streamed (SSE) responses that continue writing after that point; this was addressed separately in #3585923.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: May 6, 2026

Key contributors

  • mglaman (Acquia)
  • e0ipso (Acquia)

item.title: #3585914: Plugin subdirectory collides with Tool API on case-insensitive filesystems
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3585914 · 1 contributor · 14 comments

Summary

MCP Server previously discovered its Tool plugins under a src/Plugin/Tool/ directory. That path collides with the separate Tool API module's src/Plugin/tool/Tool/ directory on case-insensitive filesystems (macOS, Windows), since those filesystems treat Tool and tool as the same folder. A module wanting to provide both an MCP Server tool and a Tool API tool could not create both directories. To fix this, MCP Server moved all five of its plugin manager subdirectories under a module-namespaced Plugin/mcp_server/... path, following the same convention Tool API already uses.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: MCP Server plugin discovery subdirectories renamed from Plugin/Tool, Plugin/ArgumentCompletionProvider, Plugin/Notification, Plugin/ResourceProvider, and Plugin/ResourceTemplateProvider to Plugin/mcp_server/Tool, Plugin/mcp_server/ArgumentCompletionProvider, Plugin/mcp_server/Notification, Plugin/mcp_server/ResourceProvider, and Plugin/mcp_server/ResourceTemplateProvider respectively, with matching namespace changes.

Technical details

The fix updates the parent::__construct() call in each of the five plugin manager classes (ToolPluginManager, ArgumentCompletionProviderManager, NotificationProviderManager, ResourceProviderManager, ResourceTemplateProviderManager in src/Plugin/) to pass a new subdirectory argument prefixed with mcp_server, e.g. 'Plugin/Tool' becomes 'Plugin/mcp_server/Tool'. Existing plugin classes shipped in the module's own test fixtures were moved accordingly (for example tests/modules/mcp_server_test/src/Plugin/Tool/EchoTool.php moved to .../Plugin/mcp_server/Tool/EchoTool.php), and their namespace declarations were updated to match. The README's tool-authoring documentation was updated to reflect the new src/Plugin/mcp_server/Tool/ location and Drupal\my_module\Plugin\mcp_server\Tool namespace.

Upgrade

Any custom or contrib module providing plugins for MCP Server must move its plugin classes into the new subdirectories and update their namespaces:

// Before: my_module/src/Plugin/Tool/SendEmail.php
namespace Drupal\my_module\Plugin\Tool;

// After: my_module/src/Plugin/mcp_server/Tool/SendEmail.php
namespace Drupal\my_module\Plugin\mcp_server\Tool;

The same rename applies to Plugin/ArgumentCompletionProvider to Plugin/mcp_server/ArgumentCompletionProvider, Plugin/Notification to Plugin/mcp_server/Notification, Plugin/ResourceProvider to Plugin/mcp_server/ResourceProvider, and Plugin/ResourceTemplateProvider to Plugin/mcp_server/ResourceTemplateProvider. Plugins left in the old locations will no longer be discovered.

item.title: #3583014: Support example values in InputDefinitions (emit JSON Schema `examples`)
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583014 · 1 contributor · 8 comments

Summary

Tool input definitions can now carry illustrative example values, which the module emits as the standard JSON Schema examples keyword when it normalizes a tool's inputs. This helps non-deterministic callers, such as LLM function calls or MCP clients, produce well-formed values for inputs whose correct shape is not obvious from the type and description alone (formatted strings, structured maps, IDs with a specific pattern). Tools that do not set examples are unaffected: the emitted schema is byte-for-byte unchanged.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Any class implementing InputDefinitionInterface directly, rather than using InputDefinitionTrait, must now also implement getExamples() and setExamples().
  • New API: New getExamples()/setExamples() methods on InputDefinitionInterface, plus an examples constructor parameter on InputDefinition and EntityInputDefinition, to emit a JSON Schema examples keyword for an input.

Technical details

InputDefinitionTrait gains a protected array $examples property with getExamples(): array and setExamples(array $examples): static, declared on InputDefinitionInterface alongside the existing lock methods. InputDefinition and EntityInputDefinition also accept a new trailing examples constructor argument so examples can be declared directly in a #[Tool] attribute, in addition to the fluent setExamples() call for imperatively built definitions.

ContextDefinitionNormalizer::getNormalizationSchema() emits examples next to default, guarded by an InputDefinitionInterface instance check so output definitions (which don't implement the interface) are skipped. Because examples describe a single value, the emit is placed after the multiple-value array wrapping: for a multiple: TRUE input, examples land on items.examples and the array-level schema stays clean, rather than being duplicated or wrapped incorrectly. The emit reads getExamples() off the post-transform definition (after ToolInputDefinitionNormalizeEvent subscribers run), the same exposure default already has: a subscriber that swaps in a whole replacement definition (as the entity-handle subscribers do) sheds stale examples automatically, since examples only lives on InputDefinitionInterface. Examples are treated purely as annotations: they are never validated or stripped at runtime. Instead, InputExamplesEmissionTest asserts every emitted examples entry validates against its own emitted schema, catching stale or mismatched examples for first-party tools at test time.

Upgrade

Set example values on an input definition either through the attribute:

'field_name' => new InputDefinition(
  data_type: 'string',
  label: new TranslatableMarkup('Field name'),
  description: new TranslatableMarkup('The machine name of the field.'),
  examples: ['field_tags', 'field_summary'],
),

or fluently on an already built definition:

$definition->setExamples(['field_tags', 'field_summary']);

If you implement InputDefinitionInterface directly instead of using InputDefinitionTrait, add getExamples() and setExamples() to your class.

item.title: #3601362: DDEV: expose a VNC X display for non-headless agent-browser, plus optional ffmpeg session recording
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3601362 · 1 contributor · 12 comments

Summary

The one-line Drupal installer (via its configure_ddev step and the "Extra Drupal Installations" mechanism from #3601361) can now set up a virtual display you can actually watch. A new opt-in extra, "Watch the agent's browser (noVNC)", adds a DDEV add-on that runs a virtual X display and a browser-based VNC viewer inside the web container, so agent-browser can be run non-headless (--headed) and you can watch what the agent's browser is doing live, instead of only seeing whatever screenshot the agent happened to take. Headless remains the default; this is purely opt-in. The optional ffmpeg session-recording idea from the original proposal was not implemented in this change, only the required VNC display piece.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The extra, extra_agent_browser_display in src/lib/extras/extra_agent_browser_display.sh, does no installation itself: it appends a pinned add-on URL (_AGENT_BROWSER_DISPLAY_ADDON, a release-tag tarball for aivazashvilitekla/ddev-agent-browser-display) to the DDEV_ADDONS array. That array is fetched by step_install_ddev_addons (ddev add-on get) and applied by the existing add-on restart step, so this extra costs the build no extra DDEV restart. The add-on itself (external to this repo) runs Xvfb + x11vnc + noVNC as web_extra_daemons in the web container, sets DISPLAY=:99, and publishes noVNC through ddev-router on port 6080.

The pin matters because the extra hardcodes the add-on's contract, port 6080 and path /vnc.html, in the welcome text; a floating owner/repo reference could resolve to a future release whose port or path differs, so the extra warns if a config supplies a non-pinned entry for the same add-on (matched by repo name substring) while still deferring to that config's choice.

A new built-in handler, _agent_browser_display_welcome in src/lib/defaults/agent_browser_display_addon.sh, is registered on the existing ddev_addon_added event (fired only after a successful ddev add-on get) and appends the "Watch the agent's browser" line, including the {SITE_URL}:6080/vnc.html address, to APPEND_WELCOME_TEXT, which print_welcome.sh renders at the end of the build. This mirrors the pattern already used by selenium_addon.sh's _selenium_headed_rewrite. Because step_install_extras now has one more extra ahead of it, its documented pipeline slot moved from 10 to 11 (and the add-on fetch/restart slots shifted accordingly), a bookkeeping change with no behavioral effect on existing extras.

item.title: #3601383: Curated npx skills (agent-browser, drupal-module-finder, superpowers, find-skills) missing after install — lost between .claude/skills and the .agents/skills symlink
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3601383 · 1 contributor · 16 comments

Summary

one_line_installer scaffolds DDEV-based Drupal projects wired up for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode), including a curated set of default "skills" (agent-browser, drupal-module-finder, superpowers, find-skills) installed via the npx skills add CLI. item.description:

Summary

Field Validation's Regex rule lets site builders validate a field's value against a PCRE pattern. If the pattern was malformed, most commonly missing its required delimiters (a common mistake when migrating rules from Drupal 7, where delimiters were optional), the module previously let a raw PHP warning from preg_match() leak straight into the site, both while configuring the rule and later while validating real content. This is fixed: the rule's configuration form now validates the pattern up front and shows a clear, actionable error, and the pattern field's description explicitly states that the expression must include delimiters (e.g. /^[a-z0-9]+$/). As a safety net, if a bad pattern still slips through and is run against actual field data, the module now traps the underlying warning, logs it, and reports a normal validation failure instead of a PHP warning.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The fix lands in two places. RegexConstraintFieldValidationRule::validateConfigurationForm() (new) runs the submitted pattern through preg_match() under a temporary set_error_handler() that traps the E_WARNING preg_match() emits on a malformed pattern (rather than relying on the @ operator, which is unreliable across error-handler configurations); on failure it calls $form_state->setErrorByName('pattern', ...) with a message including the underlying PCRE error. Because this plugin form is nested inside FieldValidationRuleFormBase, which builds a separate FormState object for the plugin's own validateConfigurationForm() call, that base class was also changed to copy any errors recorded on the nested FormState back onto the real $form_state via setErrorByName('data][' . $name, ...), otherwise the plugin-level error would be silently swallowed.

At runtime, FieldValidationConstraintValidator::validate() and validatePropertyValue() no longer call $validator->validate() directly; they now go through a new safeValidate() helper that installs the same kind of temporary E_WARNING handler around the Symfony constraint validator call. If a warning fires (e.g. from Symfony's RegexValidator) and the validator did not already record a violation, safeValidate() logs the warning via the field_validation logger channel and adds a fallback "This value is not valid." violation, so a bad pattern saved before this fix (or introduced via config import) no longer surfaces a raw PHP warning to content editors.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">

item.title: #3471408: not_blank_constraint_rule fail on fields with multiple values
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Version: 3.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +267/−10 · php +267/−10
  • Diff: 0ea1442
  • Discussion: #3471408 · 4 contributors · 11 comments
  • Followers: 5
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 4 contributors

Summary

The Field Validation module's "not blank" rule failed to catch empty values in the middle of a multi-value field. For example, a field limited to two values where only the first was filled in would save without any validation error, even though the same rule correctly flagged the case where both values were left blank. This is now fixed: leaving any value blank in a bounded multi-value field triggers the "this value should not be blank" error, matching how the required validator behaved in Drupal 7. Two things to be aware of before upgrading: the check now runs on any save, not just form submissions, so migrations or code that creates entities programmatically with fewer values than the field allows will also start failing validation; and the error is reported at the field level rather than pointing at the specific empty value, since the widget no longer has a row to attach it to once the blank value has been stripped out.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The root cause was upstream of the validator: EntityFormDisplay::extractFormValues() calls FieldItemList::filterEmptyItems() before validation runs, stripping blank deltas and reindexing what remains. On a two-value field with only the first value filled, the second delta simply no longer exists by the time FieldValidationConstraintValidator inspects the field, so there is nothing left to flag.

The fix, in FieldValidationConstraintValidator, compares the field storage's cardinality (via FieldStorageDefinitionInterface) against $items->count(). When cardinality is bounded and greater than the number of items present, each missing delta is validated with a NULL value the same way a fully empty field already was, running any not_blank_constraint_rule (and other property constraints) against it. Unlimited-cardinality fields are left untouched, since there is no way to know how many widget rows were actually rendered for those, so padding them would produce false positives. The duplicated constraint-instantiation logic used for both the per-delta loop and the new missing-delta loop was extracted into a shared validatePropertyValue() helper. A missing delta reports its violation at the field-level property path rather than a per-delta path, because core's WidgetBase::flagErrors() looks up deltas in $field_state['original_deltas'], which no longer contains a stripped delta and throws a TypeError if a violation targets it directly.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: August 31, 2024
  • Committed: August 31, 2026 (1 year later)

Key contributors

  • marc.bau
  • abhisekmazumdar (Dropsolid)
  • ahmad-khalil-imagex (ImageX)

Collaboration

item.title: #3525460: Update symfony/expression-language to v7 (Compatibility with module_builder)
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 3.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 1 file, +1/−1 · json +1/−1
  • Diff: 3de7733
  • Discussion: #3525460 · 6 contributors · 14 comments
  • Followers: 8
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 6 contributors

Summary

Field Validation's composer.json previously pinned symfony/expression-language to ^6.3, which made it impossible to install alongside modules like module_builder that require symfony/expression-language:^7. The requirement has been widened to ^6.3 || ^7 so Composer can pick whichever major version satisfies all of a site's dependencies, removing that install-time conflict. If your site ends up resolving to v7 (because of another dependency), be aware that Symfony changed the in and not in operators in v7 to use strict comparison instead of loose comparison. This module's own code doesn't use those operators, but if you have written Expression constraint rules using in/not in, their behavior could change silently: double check them after the underlying library version changes on your site.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Requirements: composer.json now allows symfony/expression-language ^6.3 || ^7 instead of only ^6.3, resolving a conflict with modules (e.g. module_builder) that require v7.

Technical details

The fix is a one-line change to composer.json, widening symfony/expression-language from "^6.3" to "^6.3 || ^7". symfony/intl was deliberately left at ^6.3 since it wasn't part of the module_builder conflict this issue was filed to fix.

The module's own \Drupal\field_validation\Plugin\Validation\Constraint\ExpressionConstraint doesn't invoke in/not in itself, so no code changes were needed here, but the loosened constraint means the effective version of symfony/expression-language on a given site is no longer guaranteed to be v6: it depends on whatever else is installed. Under v7, in/not in comparisons became strict (e.g. '1' in [1, 2, 3] evaluates to true under v6 but false under v7), so any site-authored Expression constraint rule relying on loose comparison could behave differently depending on which major version Composer resolves.

item.title: #3601400: Management mode hangs for ~60s with no output: `ddev exec true` starts the project instead of probing it

item.title: #3601396: Handoff prompt: Enter should open the shell immediately, Esc to skip; --yolo skips the handoff entirely
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3601396 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

The one_line_installer's final step, which offers to drop you into a shell inside your freshly installed project, had its confirmation key backwards: pressing Enter used to skip the handoff, while doing nothing for 30 seconds opened the shell. This is now fixed so Enter immediately opens the shell (matching normal “Enter confirms” expectations), Esc explicitly skips it, and letting the 30 second timer run out still opens the shell. Additionally, running the installer with --yolo no longer bypasses this prompt entirely: as long as a real terminal is available, a --yolo run gets the same prompt and lands you in the project directory, since that's what a human running it interactively almost always wants. The only remaining case where the handoff is skipped automatically is when /dev/tty can't be opened at all, such as in CI or when an agent runs the installer without a pty.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The fix is in step_agent_handoff() in src/lib/steps/agent_handoff.sh. Previously it did a single IFS= read -r -t 30 </dev/tty line-read: any Enter press (success exit status) meant "skip," and only a timeout (non-zero exit) fell through to exec "${SHELL:-bash}". That logic is replaced by a new helper, _agent_handoff_read_choice(), which loops on read -rsn1 -t "$remaining" to read single keypresses against a shrinking time budget (tracked via $SECONDS so the 30s window, configurable through AGENT_HANDOFF_TIMEOUT, covers the whole wait rather than resetting per keystroke). Enter ('', $'\n', or $'\r'), a read timeout, or a read error all resolve to "open". A bare Esc ($'\e') resolves to "skip", but the function first drains up to two more bytes to distinguish a real Esc from the start of an arrow/function-key escape sequence, treating a full sequence as "any other key" that just keeps the window running. Any other key is likewise ignored and the loop continues.

The early if [[ $YOLO -eq 1 ]] || ! { : </dev/tty; } 2>/dev/null; then guard was narrowed to just the /dev/tty check, so --yolo no longer bypasses the handoff when a terminal is actually available; the timeout path already served as the unattended/--yolo fallback. The duplicated "your project is ready in ..." messaging used on both the no-tty and Esc-skip paths was factored into a new _agent_handoff_skipped() helper.
